# 2 Baruch Chapter 3 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Fall of Jerusalem

---

**1** And I answered and said: "O Lord my Lord, have I come into the world for this purpose, that I might see the evils of my mother?

**2** Not so, my Lord. If I have found grace in your sight, first take away my spirit that I may go to my fathers and not see the destruction of my mother.

**3** For two things press heavily upon me, and I am unable to endure them: for I cannot resist the wrath that has come upon Zion, and moreover I cannot endure to see the evil of my brethren who have been led into captivity.

**4** But one thing I will say before you, O Lord: What then will become of your law? Will it also be given over with Zion into captivity?

**5** Or shall the priests who ministered before you be taken away? And shall the lampstand with its light be extinguished? And shall the incense that is offered perish?

**6** And shall the daily oblations that were offered be discontinued? And shall the hymns of praise that were sung cease?

**7** And where is all that which you said to me regarding this city? Where is it now?

**8** If you destroy your city and deliver up your land to those who hate us, how shall the name of Israel be remembered?

**9** Or how shall we speak again of your praises? Or to whom shall your law be explained?"

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal rendering of Baruch's intercessory lament. "Mother" for Jerusalem is the Syriac personification. The series of rhetorical questions (vv.5-9) constitute a liturgical lament form.*
